newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Rights group says Palestinian forces use torture.
newsitem.headline: Rights group says Palestinian forces use torture.

text.p: A Palestinian human rights group said on Monday torture of prisoners was endemic in all Palestinian Authority security branches and demanded a halt to the practice.

"(It is urgent) to combat the indefensible practices of beating, whipping, tying up, burning and worse of Palestinians by other Palestinians," Bassem Eid of the Palestinian Human Rights Monitoring Group told a news conference.
"Let us ask our president, Yasser Arafat, who promised us many times to stop the practice of torture; let us ask the press: 'Where are you?'"
The Monitoring Group released a document detailing what it said were 42 cases of torture in 1996 and 1997 and said two Palestinians had been tortured to death in detention this year.
"Records are not kept," Eid said. "Some people are afraid to talk. Some are too ashamed to talk. I'm still trying to understand this reality we're now living in."
Palestinian Attorney-General Khaled al-Qidra said the report was exaggerated.

"Our laws forbid totally any kind of torture. It is not, as the report said, usual treatment in our Palestinian Authority. This is not true at all. We are interested in guaranteeing the dignity of our people," he said.

He said the Authority, which took control of parts of the West Bank and the Gaza Strip in 1994 under a peace deal with Israel, would investigate all allegations of torture and punish the perpetrators.
"It is not our habit, but perhaps a few (incidents of torture) happen here and there," al-Qidra said.
Last August, a Palestinian military court sentenced three Palestinian policemen to long jail terms after it found them guilty of torturing a prisoner to death.
Eid said the Authority primarily uses torture to obtain confessions in many criminal investigations and also to force witnesses to testify.
He also accused the Palestinian government of lacking control over its security forces and responding slowly when torture is reported or suspected.

The brother of Yussuf al-Baba, a 32-year-old who Palestinian officials acknowledged was tortured to death this year while in detention over land deals, told the news conference Palestinian authorities ignored the family's request for a medical report.

"They said, 'After you bury him, we will give you the report,'" said Omar al-Baba. "But after we buried him, they didn't give us any reports. When we went to get the report, they kicked us out and they cursed at us."
